newsitem.title: USA: Morgan buying mutual fund firm stake for $900 million.
newsitem.headline: Morgan buying mutual fund firm stake for $900 million.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co. said Wednesday it agreed to pay $900 million for a 45 percent stake in American Century Cos., the nation's fourth-largest mutual fund company, in a bid to expand its financial services business.
Morgan, the fourth largest banking company, said the two companies would form a new partnership to market pension plans such as 401(k) plans to corporations and individual investors.
Industry analysts said the move would speed the growth of Morgan's investment management business and probably make it more profitable as well.

"The general thought with J.P. Morgan is that it has too much dependence on lower-margin business with white shoe companies," said one analyst who asked not to be identified. "They need to take actions such as this, and probably more."
Doing business with the big corporate customers "does not always result in high profit margins," the analyst said.
The retirement plan business that Morgan wants to expand is one of the fastest-growing in the financial services industry, analysts said.
The growth prospects of that business helped drive the $11 billion merger of Morgan Stanley & Co. Inc. and Dean Witter Discover & Co. earlier this year.
Morgan said the purchase of the American Century stake will give it retail mutual fund distribution, products and technology that complement its traditional focus on institutional investors.
Morgan, which is based in New York, also said it plans to offer financial services to individuals, focusing on the wealthy.

American Century, a no-load mutual fund company based in Kansas City, Mo., that sells directly to individuals, manages $60 billion in assets in about 70 mutual funds. Morgan manages $234 billion, about 10 percent of it in mutual funds.
Morgan Chairman Douglas Warner III said the partnership will accelerate the company's asset management business by adding service and product expertise, distribution and technology.

The analyst who requested anonymity said J.P. Morgan had telegraphed its move in at the annual meeting in May, when Warner said investment management was one areas where the company wanted to expand. The company has been making similar statments to analysts for some time.
James Stowers Jr., founder of American Century, and his family will retain voting control of the company, the companies said.

Morgan also said it will have an option to raise its stake in American Century. In addition, two Morgan executives, Ramon de Oliveira and Edward Kelly III, will join American Century's board of directors.
The companies expect the deal to close in four to six months.
Morgan stock rose $1.375 to $115.625 in consolidated midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
